# Chapter 1: Rules

## Board and pieces
Place the board so each player has a light square on the right. Put the queen on her own color and the king beside her.

## Objective
Win by checkmate. The game is drawn by stalemate, insufficient material, threefold repetition, or the fifty-move rule.

## Legal moves
Pawns move forward one square, or two from their starting row, and capture diagonally. They may promote on the last rank. Knights jump in an L-shape. Bishops, rooks, queens, and kings move along diagonals, ranks, files, or one square, respectively.

## Castling
A player may castle only if the king and chosen rook have not moved, no pieces stand between them, and the king is not in check, does not pass through check, and does not end in check.

## Touch-move rule
If you touch a piece, you must move it if it has a legal move. Say “I adjust” before rearranging a piece.

## Clock
Press your clock after every move. If time expires, the opponent wins if material can force mate; otherwise the game is drawn unless an illegal move caused the timeout.

## Worked examples
1. White: e2–e4. Legal pawn advance.
2. Black: Nf6xe4. Legal knight capture.
3. White: O–O. Legal if f1 and g1 are empty and e1, f1, g1 are not attacked.
4. White plays b2–b4; Black’s pawn on c3 may capture b2 en passant.

## Club rules
Be respectful, avoid distractions, no phone use, no unauthorized help, and follow the tournament director’s decisions.
